owasp_coverage: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
summary: The D4/D10 defense-in-depth architecture is sound. auth.ts implementation (timingSafeEqual with zero-padding) is correctly implemented. Two issues require fixes: (1) missing .gitignore risks committing MNEMONIC_IDENTITY private key and MEMORY_API_KEY to git — high severity, (2) nginx auth bypass when MEMORY_API_KEY is empty string — medium severity that could affect misconfigured deployments. No critical vulnerabilities found.

findings.title: No .gitignore: MNEMONIC_IDENTITY private key and MEMORY_API_KEY can be accidentally committed
findings.description: The repository has no .gitignore file. MNEMONIC_IDENTITY contains an Ed25519 private key JSON, MNEMONIC_JWT is a signed JWT, and MEMORY_API_KEY is the sole authentication token. All three are stored in .env. An `git add .` or `git add .env` would commit them in plaintext. The .env.example comment warns against this but there's no technical enforcement.
findings.attack_scenario: Developer runs `git add . && git commit` → .env committed → pushed to GitHub → private key and API key exposed. Ed25519 private key cannot be rotated after exposure; all previously signed attestations remain valid under the compromised key.
findings.recommendation:
Create /home/op/Projects/universal-memory/.gitignore with at minimum:
```
.env
.env.local
*.env
!.env.example
node_modules/
/tmp/
```
Also add to .dockerignore: `*.env` is already there via `.env.*` ✓

findings.title: nginx auth bypass when MEMORY_API_KEY is empty string
findings.description: Line 65: `if ($http_authorization = "Bearer $memory_api_key")`. If /etc/nginx/memory-secrets.conf sets `$memory_api_key` to an empty string (e.g. operator creates the file but forgets to set the value, or sets it to `""`), then the condition becomes `if ($http_authorization = "Bearer ")`. An attacker sending `Authorization: Bearer ` (Bearer with trailing space) would match this condition and bypass authentication.
findings.attack_scenario: Operator creates /etc/nginx/memory-secrets.conf with `set $memory_api_key "";` as a placeholder → nginx starts successfully → attacker discovers the endpoint (e.g. via DNS enumeration) → sends `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ' https://memory.example.com/mcp` → reaches memory-hub → memory-hub's validateBearer() rejects empty token (empty string !== expected key even with zero-padding) → 401 from memory-hub. The defense-in-depth at memory-hub saves this case ✓, but nginx still lets it through.

findings.title: No rate limiting — brute-force attack on Bearer token possible at nginx level
findings.description: There is no `limit_req_zone` or `limit_conn_zone` directive. An attacker can send unlimited Authorization requests at network speed. While memory-hub's timingSafeEqual prevents timing-based attacks on individual comparisons, high-volume brute-force (millions of requests/second) is still possible if the 64-char hex key space is smaller than assumed. A 32-byte (64-char hex) key from `openssl rand -hex 32` has 2^256 entropy — brute force is computationally infeasible — but the absence of rate limiting also enables DoS attacks.
findings.recommendation:
Add to nginx.conf (http context, not inside server block):
```nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=memory_api:10m rate=10r/m;
```
Then inside the server block:
```nginx
limit_req zone=memory_api burst=5 nodelay;
```
This limits to 10 requests/minute per IP with a burst of 5, returning 429 on excess. Adjust rate based on legitimate usage patterns.

findings.title: server_tokens not disabled — nginx version disclosed in error responses
findings.description: nginx default behavior includes the version number in Server response headers and error pages (e.g. `Server: nginx/1.25.3`). This allows attackers to fingerprint the exact nginx version and check for known CVEs.
findings.recommendation:
Add to the server block:
```nginx
server_tokens off;
```
This replaces `Server: nginx/1.25.3` with `Server: nginx`.

findings.title: Content-Type: application/json add_header at server level overwrites upstream Content-Type
findings.description: Line 117 adds Content-Type: application/json to ALL server responses including proxied MCP SSE streams (which should be text/event-stream). This is both a functional bug (breaks SSE) and a mild security concern (incorrect MIME types can affect browser handling). Note: this is primarily a functional issue, escalated from code-reviewer, confirmed from security perspective.
findings.recommendation: Remove line 117. The 401 response from `return 401 '...'` body does not need this because nginx will send it with text/html by default — but clients parsing JSON won't care about Content-Type for 401 errors. If strictly needed, move into the error if-block only.

findings.owasp: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: No nginx access_log configuration — 401 events not explicitly structured for monitoring
findings.description: nginx uses its default `combined` log format. Authentication failures (401s) are logged, but the log format doesn't include response time or upstream status. For a single-user deployment this is acceptable, but a structured log format with status codes would enable better monitoring of auth failure patterns.

findings.title: timingSafeEqual with zero-padding is correctly implemented
findings.description: The auth.ts implementation correctly handles the timingSafeEqual requirement: both buffers are zero-padded to max(len_a, len_b) before comparison, and a separate `lengthsMatch` boolean prevents false positives from zero-padded shorter tokens. D13 is correctly enforced: no token values appear in logs.

findings.title: Secrets correctly passed as runtime env vars (not baked into image)
findings.description: MEMORY_API_KEY, MNEMONIC_IDENTITY, and MNEMONIC_JWT are passed via the `environment:` section of docker-compose.yml referencing .env file variables. They are NOT baked into the Docker image via ARG/ENV Dockerfile directives, which would expose them in `docker history` and image layers.

findings.title: Postgres port not exposed to host — only accessible inside Docker network
findings.description: The postgres service uses `expose: 5432` (not `ports:`). This means Postgres is unreachable from outside the Docker network, preventing direct connection attacks against the database. memory-hub connects via the internal Docker DNS name `postgres:5432`.
